newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms on tight liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms on tight liquidity.

text.p: Indonesia's rupiah remained firm against the dollar in moderate late trading on Friday on the back of continued tight market liquidity, dealers said.
One bank dealer said state-owned banks appeared to have been active in the market, pushing the overnight swap rate higher.
"State-owned banks were seen actively trading short-term swaps, particularly overnight swaps, due to weekly tax payments and the end of reporting period," the dealer said.
The dealer, however, said the local currency's upward trend was limited due to earlier speculation of a higher fixing rate later on Friday.
The U.S. bank dealer said the spot rupiah rate was likely to range between 2,353.00 and 2,354.00 on Monday.
Spot rupiah was last quoted at 2,353.20/53.50 against an opening of 2,354.00/54.25.
Tomorrow and today rupiah were last quoted at 2,352.95/53.05 and 2,350.95/51.75, respectively.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by another one point to 2,352/2,544 and the conversion band to 2,352/2,400 late on Friday as anticipated earlier.
The central bank had previously increased the fixing rate by three points this week.
Overnight swap was last at 1.85/1.95 from an opening of 1.50/1.60 while tom/next was last at 0.45/0.55 against an opening of 0.40/0.48.
One-month swap was at 14.50/15.50, two at 30.25/31.00, three at 43.00/43.75 and six at 86.00/87.00 points.
